title: Chat-led first-user setup audit
method: Source-only inspection. No service was launched, model downloaded, permission granted, or production state changed. Findings describe the checked-out source, not a verified native runtime.
overall: A blank user cannot currently rely on Chat to drive setup end to end. The first usable Chat turn needs an already configured language model; the no-model wizard path intentionally enters the app with Chat unable to reply. Once Chat works, Developer shell and browser tools can attempt machine setup, but Model Manager cannot download or select a new model, Desktop Control is off by default and has no first-class settings control, and Tailscale guidance conflicts with the current loopback-plus-Serve architecture.

evidence.finding: BootScreen classifies backend config and offers retry/unpaired states; wizard is entered only after a valid config response.

Model step supports hosted key test, Ollama status/start/pull/check, and Decide later; Review explicitly warns Chat cannot reply without a model. Completion persists identity and wizard_complete, with Retry or Continue anyway on save error.

Chat creates a session and sends a normal agent turn; no deterministic setup-only responder is present in this path. Session creation itself has no configured-provider gate, so a session may exist even while no inference can answer.

Developer shell is enabled by default; browser open_website exists. Desktop Control provides macOS AX status/apps/tree/click/type, but the extension and its flag default off and macOS Accessibility remains an OS grant.

Agent Model Manager exposes list_models and propose_model_upgrade for already installed GGUF registry models. Settings has a separate GGUF download/cancel UI and the wizard has an Ollama pull path. The agent tool neither pulls Ollama nor downloads GGUF, and list_models is not an Ollama inventory.

Settings Devices can read tailnet and Serve status, toggle Serve, create a one-time pairing link, and show devices. Its setup button copies a request to clipboard and opens Chat; it does not prefill/send or begin a durable setup task.

Developer shell and desktop action tool annotations are mutating/open-world, and Decision Inbox has tool approval evidence/actions; an explicit setup-specific approval for installs, external login, Accessibility, or network exposure is not represented as a coherent workflow.

blocking_gaps.problem: No-provider bootstrap is a chicken-and-egg: after Decide later, Chat cannot answer a request to set up its own first model. An optional first message is only stashed in the composer; it is not an offline setup executor.
blocking_gaps.fix: Provide a deterministic setup assistant/launcher outside inference, reachable from the empty Chat state and wizard Review. It should inspect status, guide model/provider setup, invoke existing bounded setup endpoints only on explicit user action, and hand off to Chat only after a live provider check. Keep a direct Settings path.

blocking_gaps.problem: Device self-knowledge still instructs HOST=0.0.0.0 and claims the user's only step is one login click. Current backend intentionally uses loopback plus tailscale serve; companion pairing and Serve activation remain separate steps.
blocking_gaps.fix: Update the Devices feature descriptor, teaching text, snapshots and generated prompt to say: detect/install/sign in, enable Serve on explicit user action, verify Serve URL and hub reachability, create pairing link, then complete pairing on the companion. Never recommend 0.0.0.0. Include install/login/account prompts as user-owned boundaries.

blocking_gaps.problem: Settings' 'Have agent set it up' button silently writes a long instruction to clipboard then opens Chat. The user must paste/send it, and the button can appear when Chat has no provider. It promises terminal execution without showing prerequisites or subsequent result.
blocking_gaps.fix: Replace clipboard side effect with a visible, editable setup request in Chat when ready, or route to the deterministic setup surface when no provider. Preserve user send as the initiating action. Show current Tailscale and Serve states before and after, with Retry and Cancel.

blocking_gaps.problem: Model Manager language suggests stewardship but its only mutation proposes a switch to an already installed GGUF model; it cannot fetch a model and cannot cover Ollama. A generic 'download/configure models' request therefore falls back to unconstrained shell commands despite existing bounded HTTP routes.
blocking_gaps.fix: Expose a narrow, source-specific model setup capability to the agent: read installed/downloadable inventory for Ollama and GGUF, initiate a user-approved download, report durable job progress, cancel, verify checksum/installed state and live inference, then propose or set the chat route with explicit approval. Keep separate sources visibly distinct.

blocking_gaps.problem: Ollama wizard progress is tied to one SSE response. Aborting on unmount cancels the client connection and is described as stopped, but the UI has no authoritative server job status or cancellation receipt; a stream error event can be swallowed as non-progress, and EOF need not mean verified installed.
blocking_gaps.fix: Make download a server-owned job with job ID, status/progress/error, idempotent retry and explicit cancel endpoint. On completion re-read installed inventory and run the live provider check before saying Ready. Restore status after navigation/restart.
blocking_gaps.post_audit_outcome: A narrower frontend fix now surfaces SSE error events and application error payloads, cancels/releases the client reader on parser or callback error, checks fresh installed inventory after stream EOF before claiming the model is installed, and labels abort as Stop waiting because the server may continue. A separate live provider check remains required before Ready. Wizard/API focused tests passed 16/16; command-center TypeScript and production build passed with bounded Node 24. Server-owned durable jobs, authoritative cancellation, restart recovery, and a live download remain unimplemented or unverified. See DESIGN_INTERACTION_AUDIT_2026-10-09.json post_audit_validation.

blocking_gaps.problem: Desktop Control is disabled at two layers and no explicit Settings control was found. The agent can report the flag and macOS Accessibility state but cannot truthfully promise computer use from blank setup. AX click/type is also a limited action set, not general screenshot-based computer use.
blocking_gaps.fix: Add a clearly scoped Settings permission card explaining local AX control, its limits, the runtime switch, OS grant, current status, and revocation. Require direct user action to enable; recheck OS status before each action. Offer a link to macOS Accessibility settings and a test action with observable result.

blocking_gaps.problem: Wizard Review marks a model 'connected' from configured-provider registry state, rather than a fresh live readiness result. Hosted test explicitly allows an inconclusive check and local test has a fallback when check result is absent.
blocking_gaps.fix: Use explicit saved/configured/tested/unverified/ready states in Review and empty Chat. Do not call a provider Ready until a successful live check; if verification is unavailable, say it will be tested on first send and expose Retry.

blocking_gaps.problem: The wizard offers Ollama only if its provider is present in the registry. The standalone GGUF runtime is available later in Settings, so a user who wants all-local inference sees two different setups without an explanatory bridge.
blocking_gaps.fix: Present one 'On this Mac' choice with two clearly labeled engines only when both are actually supported, or choose one recommended engine with a concise advanced link. Base choices on backend capability and RAM/disk evidence rather than a provider-list proxy.

smallest_coherent_sequence: 1. Fix the false Tailscale runbook and Devices button copy/action first; remove 0.0.0.0 guidance and distinguish install, login, Serve, link creation and companion claim.

2. Add a deterministic no-model setup controller and Chat empty state that reads real provider/Ollama/GGUF status and can open existing wizard/Settings actions. This is the bootstrapping path; do not ask a model that does not exist to install itself.

3. Define a single setup operation state contract (kind, phase, capability, progress, evidence, error, cancelability) persisted server-side for long installs/downloads. Reuse it from wizard, Settings and Chat, with explicit user approval at install/account/OS/network boundaries.

4. Add narrow agent-callable adapters for model and device status/actions with structured receipts. Keep shell as a fallback for diagnosed exceptions, never as the only source of progress truth. Wire navigation to the relevant Settings pane and Decision Inbox.

5. Integrate readiness labels in Review, Settings and Chat from the same live checks. Add recoverable failure states and resume-on-relaunch, then verify a real end-to-end path in a guarded isolated root.
ui_guidance: Use a small number of user-centered stages: Choose brain, Make it ready, Connect devices, Ready. Show the current state and next action rather than a console transcript.

Make each operation's source, expected disk/network effect, user-owned approval, current progress and verifiable outcome visible. A spinner is not evidence of installation; a live check or detected OS state is.
Use platform-native permission phrasing and standard macOS Settings navigation. Do not imply the app can grant Accessibility or approve a Tailscale login on the user's behalf.
Keep primary action singular and reversible where possible; Cancel and Retry remain in the same context. Preserve the entered provider/model choice through Back, failure and relaunch.
State the boundary between this Mac and other devices plainly: Tailscale sign-in, Serve availability, and per-device pairing are distinct verified steps.
independent_acceptance_tests: Fresh isolated config, no provider, no Ollama and no GGUF: wizard can finish with Decide later; Chat shows unable-to-reply state plus working deterministic setup action; attempting ordinary send does not claim an agent reply or initiate an unapproved install.
Hosted key path: invalid key stays unverified, inconclusive result stays unverified, valid live check becomes ready; credential value never appears in logs, reports, tool transcripts or Review.

Local model path with fake backend: start missing runtime, approve a download, observe server-owned monotonic progress, cancel, relaunch, retry/resume, verify installed inventory and a live inference check before Ready; simulated stream EOF without model remains failure.

Device path with fake Tailscale executable: absent, installed/disconnected, login pending, Running without DNS, Running with DNS but Serve off, Serve on, and Serve error each yield distinct next actions. No path instructs 0.0.0.0 or claims pairing before a companion token is redeemed.

Desktop Control matrix: extension disabled, flag off, macOS permission absent and fully granted each produce accurate status; click/type refuse without gates; secure fields remain redacted/refused; user can revoke and subsequent actions fail closed.

Approval path: install, external account login, model download/storage, Serve exposure and AX enable each show concrete scope and wait for the relevant direct user or OS decision. Deny/cancel leaves configuration unchanged and supports retry.

Navigation path: Devices setup CTA transfers a visible editable request or opens deterministic setup, never a silent clipboard-only intent; Chat, Settings and Review show the same readiness after restart.

Native guarded smoke test: first-run root, no user data, no live installation/network grants, then a consented test fixture covering provider readiness, model job lifecycle, Tailscale Serve and companion claim; record direct endpoint evidence rather than seeded screenshot inference.
limits: No native binary, daemon or model turn was executed in this audit; existing screenshots and prior reports were treated as context, not proof of blank-root behavior.

This report does not claim all mutating shell commands bypass approval. Tool annotations and Decision Inbox machinery exist; exact runtime approval behavior depends on the configured permission mode and should be exercised in acceptance tests.
